meta.name: IT Service Management
meta.origin: kalita/frameworks — curated by Kalita Forge, reviewed by Architect Pro + Security Pro (product mission A)

vocabulary.meaning: Unplanned disruption or degradation of a service
Change Advisory Board — the body that approves changes
A knowledge base article that records a solution

fields.name: sla_deadline
fields.note: from the SLA policy and business calendar

roles.name: EndUser
roles.note: creates incidents/requests via the portal, sees only their own

roles.name: ServiceDeskAgent
roles.note: triage, assignment, diagnosis using the knowledge base

stages.what: an incident with source and priority
categorization, assignment to OperatorL2, linking a knowledge article
diagnosis and resolution; the SLA timer runs
confirmation of the resolution; auto-close for monitoring-sourced ones
recording the solution in Knowledge after closing
description of the change and risk

segregation_of_duties.rule: The implementer of a change does not approve it themselves (CAB gate)
The agent assigns and diagnoses, but does not close incidents without confirmation (close — HITL, or auto only for monitoring)

control_points.what: computed from SLAPolicy on the business calendar; a breach is visible on the dashboard and escalates
a Change requires ChangeManager sign-off before implement
only for incidents from monitoring (the machine does not close itself for people)
a resolution without knowledge = lost knowledge; a reminder

kpis.label: Share of incidents with an SLA breach

risks.mitigation: sla_deadline computed + dashboard + escalation on approach
deny on close for the agent (except monitoring-auto)

required.question: What counts as an incident for you?
required.why: The incident/request boundary determines the entities and SLA

required.question: Who resolves incidents — your own team or a contractor?
required.why: Determines the roles and HITL gates

important.question: Are there SLAs by priority (response/resolution hours)?
important.why: SLA is the core of ITSM; the default is sensible, but better to ask

important.question: Is change control (CAB) needed?
important.why: Changes without control are the main source of outages

important.question: Do users create requests themselves (portal) or through the service desk?

optional.question: Is there monitoring that should create incidents?
optional.why: Adds an inbound integration and auto-close; can be deferred

optional.question: Do you maintain a knowledge base?
optional.why: Adds the Knowledge entity and reminders; can be deferred

alternatives.tradeoffs: only incidents and SLA; add changes later

anti_patterns.why: SLA without a timer and dashboard is not an SLA, but a promise
changes without HITL are statistically the main cause of incidents
resolution confirmation belongs to a human

regulatory.note: For regulated industries — change management policies may be mandatory

automations.what: an incident with no movement — escalation to Supervisor
monitoring-sourced incidents close automatically after resolution
a reminder to record knowledge after closing

agent_roles.name: ServiceDeskAgent
agent_roles.note: triage and diagnosis; decisions belong to people
